title: Sjögren disease
diseaseDescription: Bounded primary Sjögren disease: epithelial activation, interferon, BAFF/B-cell activity, autoantibodies, ectopic lymphoid organisation and glandular dysfunction; excludes secondary disease, mimics and symptomatic therapy efficacy. Cross-study synthesis; incomplete lacrimal, genetic, stromal and extraglandular coverage. No universal causal loop is asserted.
releaseNote: Agent source-checked local candidate; abstract access dominates. Contradictory AQP5 evidence and BAFF null comparisons retained. Scientific domain review and calibration pending.

entities.label: Plasmacytoid DCs
entities.description: Type I interferon-producing dendritic cells; human tissue observations and mouse depletion experiments are distinguished.

entities.label: IFN-α / type I IFN
entities.description: Type I interferon responses in Sjögren tissue and experimental systems.

entities.label: IFN-γ
entities.description: Type II interferon studied in salivary epithelial cultures.

entities.label: Salivary gland epithelium
entities.description: Salivary epithelial cells studied in primary cultures and human gland tissue.

entities.label: BAFF / BLyS
entities.description: B-cell activating factor; epithelial inducibility, B-cell regulation and disease associations are context dependent.

entities.label: B cells
entities.description: B lymphocytes in glandular infiltrates and BAFF experimental models.

entities.label: Ectopic germinal centres
entities.description: Organised glandular lymphoid structures detected in a subset of patients.

entities.label: Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB
entities.description: Autoantibodies associated with RNA-binding antigens; not assumed pathogenic in every patient.

entities.label: Apoptotic material
entities.description: Material from necrotic or late apoptotic cells used in human-cell interferon-induction assays.

entities.label: Nucleic-acid immune complexes
entities.description: RNA-containing immune complexes implicated by patient-serum and cell experiments.

entities.label: GZMK+ CD8+ T cells
entities.description: Glandular T-cell population associated with disease severity and epithelial engagement.

entities.label: Granzyme K
entities.description: Effector molecule that activates epithelial interferon signalling in the inspected in-vitro study.

entities.label: Seromucous acinar-cell loss
entities.description: Selective depletion of PRR4+CST3+WFDC2-negative acinar cells observed in human salivary tissue.

entities.label: Aquaporin-5 distribution
entities.description: Subcellular localisation of the AQP5 water channel; studies disagree about abnormal localisation in Sjögren glands.

entities.label: Salivary secretory dysfunction
entities.description: Reduced saliva secretion; experimental models and human tissue associations are not interchangeable.

entities.label: Dry eyes / dry mouth
entities.description: Clinical sicca manifestations; direct lacrimal mechanisms remain incompletely curated.

claims.text: IFN-alpha induced BAFF secretion in cultured salivary epithelial cells from primary Sjögren patients and controls.
limitations: Eight patients and eight controls; culture secretion is not clinical disease causation or treatment benefit. Patient-control differences were not significant.

claims.text: IFN-gamma induced BAFF secretion in primary salivary epithelial cultures.
limitations: Same culture cohort as IFN-alpha result; not independent replication.

claims.text: Salivary epithelial cells expressed and secreted BAFF after interferon stimulation.
limitations: Induced production in culture; basal secretion was undetectable. Exact epithelial origin and stimulation methods inspected in PMC1526588 Results.

claims.text: BAFF protein secretion after interferon stimulation did not significantly differ between primary Sjögren and control cultures.
limitations: No significant patient-control difference; different within-group P values do not establish a between-group difference.

claims.text: IFN-producing plasmacytoid dendritic cells were detected in primary Sjögren salivary glands.
limitations: Tissue detection does not identify the exclusive source of type I IFN or establish temporal initiation.

claims.text: Interferons modulated IFN-inducible genes in salivary gland epithelial cells in vitro.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; study methods and controls beyond the inspected material remain unverified. Observations do not establish disease-wide causality.

claims.text: The BAFF-transgenic study identifies BAFF as a regulator of B-lymphocyte proliferation and survival.
limitations: BAFF regulation is stated in the primary report abstract; the proposed autoreactive-cell tolerance checkpoint mechanism remains an interpretation, not a demonstrated complete human circuit.

claims.text: Aged BAFF-transgenic mice developed sialadenitis with decreased saliva production.
limitations: Engineered BAFF overexpression; not evidence of sufficiency or necessity in primary human Sjögren disease.

claims.text: Glandular germinal-centre-like structures contained organised T- and B-cell aggregates with proliferating cells and follicular dendritic-cell networks.
limitations: 17% had GC-like structures; abstract does not resolve primary versus associated disease for every participant. Morphology does not establish a universal disease stage.

claims.text: Local anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB autoantibody production was increased in biopsies with germinal-centre development.
limitations: Subset association, not proof that ectopic GCs are necessary for all serum autoantibodies. Primary-only composition unresolved in abstract.

claims.text: Soluble BAFF correlated with anti-La/SSB antibodies in the inspected primary Sjögren cohort.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; study methods and controls beyond the inspected material remain unverified. Observations do not establish disease-wide causality.

claims.text: BAFF and BAFF-R glandular expression was numerically higher in GC-positive primary Sjögren patients, without a significant difference from GC-negative patients.
limitations: Null group comparison; higher serum BAFF occurred in GC-negative patients. This is not evidence that greater BAFF causes GC formation.

claims.text: Serum BAFF was higher in GC-negative than GC-positive patients, qualifying a simple BAFF-to-GC progression model.
limitations: Small mixed control/patient sample; serum and glandular compartments differ.

claims.text: Autoantibodies to RNA-binding proteins combined with dying-cell material formed an interferon-inducing system consistent with RNA-containing immune complexes.
limitations: Does not establish that every anti-SSA/SSB specificity is pathogenic. Complex-mediated interpretation is from the inspected abstract.

claims.text: Necrotic or late apoptotic cell material contributed to the patient-serum interferon-inducing immune-complex system.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; study methods and controls beyond the inspected material remain unverified. Observations do not establish disease-wide causality.

claims.text: RNA-containing immune complexes activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells through RNA-dependent and Fc-gamma-RIIa-associated processes in culture.
limitations: Culture mechanism; assembled positive feedback with epithelial BAFF and local antibodies remains a cross-study hypothesis.

claims.text: Early pDC depletion impeded secretory dysfunction in female NOD mice.
limitations: Pre-onset mouse intervention; no evidence that established human secretory loss is reversible by pDC depletion.

claims.text: Human Sjögren glands showed both a rise in GZMK-positive CD8 T cells and selective loss of a seromucous acinar population.
limitations: Co-occurrence and spatial localisation do not establish that these cells kill this acinar population in vivo.

claims.text: Glandular GZMK-positive CD8 T cells displayed a cytotoxic transcriptional program and degranulated on ex-vivo stimulation.
limitations: GZMK-defined cell identity and degranulation do not prove that GZMK directly causes in-vivo acinar-cell loss.

claims.text: Functional assays found that GZMK activates epithelial interferon signalling in vitro.
limitations: Abstract-level in-vitro evidence; does not prove systemic interferon production or clinical causality.

claims.text: Selective seromucous acinar-cell loss was part of epithelial remodeling observed in human Sjögren glands.
limitations: Anatomical association; secretory consequences were not quantified by this atomic finding.

claims.text: One small primary Sjögren biopsy study reported AQP5 redistribution from apical toward basal acinar membranes.
limitations: Small immunohistochemistry study; a separate primary study did not reproduce altered distribution.

claims.text: A separate primary Sjögren study found no difference in AQP5 distribution or density relative to controls.
limitations: Conflicting human tissue findings; AQP5 mislocalisation is not a settled universal mechanism.

claims.text: The inspected primary report notes that salivary gland dysfunction may occur without glandular destruction.
limitations: Abstract contextual statement, not a quantified within-cohort functional analysis; does not establish a causal acinar-loss pathway.

claims.text: The primary Sjögren trial describes dry eyes and mouth as clinical manifestations of the disease being studied.
limitations: Descriptive clinical linkage, not an experimental test of salivary-to-lacrimal causation. Dry-eye mechanisms are an explicit curation gap.

contexts.stage: Cross-sectional human disease and pre-onset/aged mouse systems; not a temporal disease sequence
